title: Unmeasured Network Frame Batching
pattern: Manually delaying and buffering outgoing network writes in application code before calling `write()` on a TCP socket.
why_bad: The operating system network stack already manages write buffering and TCP packet aggregation (using Nagle's algorithm). Custom user-level buffering delays packets, spikes latency, and degrades network throughput [474, 495].
detection: The presence of buffers or queues accumulating small diagnostic payloads before triggering network socket flushes.
counterexample: Zero-copy user-space network bypass stacks (like DPDK) where the operating system network layer is completely bypassed. `Contextual`.
fix: Write directly to the TCP stream using standard system calls, allowing the kernel to optimize packet flow dynamically.
